answer_key.documented_root_cause: Rotor bars separated from laminations (clean separation on one side, breach plus heat discoloration on the other) — confirmed by teardown; the separation is the cause of the vibration signature.
answer_key.note: HELD OUT — never include in session input. Teardown is the confirmation step; diagnosis-time evidence is IR thermography plus vibration only.
answer_key.repair_performed: New rotor installed in the existing stator (about $3,000 of the $7,200 assembly). Author notes that undetected, the pump would have lost the stator and risked an atmospheric release.

caveats: Teardown is the confirmation step, so diagnosis-time evidence is IR plus vibration only — the teardown finding is held out in the answer key, not an observation.

machine.description: Sealless, self-contained chemical pump, 3 HP; rotor plus stator assembly about $7,200

pass_criteria: Ranked hypotheses reach the electrical root cause (rotor-bar separation) behind a thermal trip — the cause is not the thermal protection device itself.
If the system cannot reach the root cause, it says 'unavailable with ranked guesses' honestly.
scoring.rule: Hand-run session test; tests composition only, not ingestion, binding, or the twin. Multi-evidence test: IR thermography plus vibration spectrum must be combined.

session_observations.evidence: Reliable Plant case study (Dow Corning sealless pump).
session_observations.observation: Pump trips on thermal load protection.
Process conditions apparently normal: valve positions, pressure, and flow all normal.
Infrared thermography shows a hot spot in the stator/rotor despite flush flow to the rear bearing.
Vibration spectrum shows multiple harmonics of run speed surrounded by 2x slip frequency.
Run speed 3,466 RPM versus 3,450 RPM optimum.

source.document: Reliable Plant, Dow Corning sealless pump case study
source.verified: Research report 2026-11-16, checked against the live document

symptom: Pump tripping on thermal load protection.
